newsitem.title: USA: Standard Pacific Q2 up on deliveries,margins.
newsitem.headline: Standard Pacific Q2 up on deliveries,margins.

text.p: Standard Pacific Corp Wednesday attributed stronger second-quarter earnings to increased deliveries and higher margins from the company's California homebuilding operations.
The company reported second-quarter income from continuing operations of $4,774,000, or $0.16 per share, compared with $2,198,000, or $0.07 per share, for the 1996 second quarter.
The company's Northern California, San Diego and Ventura County divisions reported a combined 24 percent increase in unit deliveries.

Although company-wide orders for the quarter were down approximately eight percent from the second quarter of 1996, the company said it ended the quarter with a backlog of 714 homes, an 18 percent increase over the year earlier period and the highest second quarter level since 1989.
The dollar value of the second quarter backlog rose 36 percent to $229.4 million.

The company attributed the lower level of new home orders primarily to higher than expected orders in the fourth quarter of 1996 and the first quarter of 1997, which reduced the company's inventory of homes available for sale in the second quarter of 1997.
The average selling price increased 14 percent because of a greater distribution of homes delivered in the $400,000 to $800,000 price range in California, the company said.
Homebuilding gross margins increased to 15.0 percent in the second quarter from 12.4 percent in the 1996 second quarter and 14.1 percent in the 1997 first quarter.
The company said it is beginning to see a recovery in the San Diego housing market. It plans 10 to 12 new projects in California through the end of the year.
